summary: An inventory lists the files in a folder of research data, with their sizes, formats and table columns, and never what is in them; you make it on your own computer, and your data never leave it.

systems.name: Windows
systems.terminal: Open PowerShell: select Start, type PowerShell and press Enter.

systems.name: macOS
systems.terminal: Open Terminal: press Command and Space, type Terminal and press Return.

systems.name: Linux
systems.terminal: Open a terminal. On a server or a cluster, sign in to it as you usually do.

steps.install: Install uv, a tool that installs and runs Python programs. You need do this only once. Then close the terminal and open a new one, so that it finds uv.
steps.run: Run the inventory, replacing the path with the folder that holds your data. On your own computer you can drag the folder onto the terminal to type its path.
steps.after: It writes inventory.json in the folder where you ran it. A large dataset can take a while, because every file is read to compute its digest. The command sends nothing anywhere.
